text: EDR: Ransomware behavior. WINWORD.EXE spawned cmd.exe, which ran 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet' on WS-HR-03.
label: escalate
why: Deleting volume shadow copies from a Word child process is a standard pre-encryption step (ATT&CK T1490). Isolate the host now.

text: Brute force: 240 failed logons (4625) for j.martin on VPN-GW-01 from 192.0.2.44 in 12 minutes, followed by a successful logon (4624) from the same IP.
label: escalate
why: Hundreds of failures and then a success from the same external IP means the password was guessed. The account is now in an attacker's hands.

text: EDR detection 'OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory'. procdump64.exe, run from C:\Users\Public, opened lsass.exe with read access and wrote lsass.dmp.
label: escalate
why: A memory dump of LSASS holds the credentials of everyone logged on. A sysinternals tool run from a world-writable folder by a service account is not maintenance (T1003.001).

text: CloudTrail: ConsoleLogin success for the root user without MFA from 203.0.113.77, followed within 4 minutes by CreateAccessKey and PutBucketPolicy granting Principal '*' read on s3://acme-payroll-exports.
label: escalate
why: HARD CASE (no keywords). Root should never sign in day to day, never without MFA, and a new access key plus a public bucket policy on payroll data is persistence and exposure in one step.

text: EDR telemetry: OUTLOOK.EXE spawned mshta.exe with a remote .hta URL; mshta.exe then made an outbound HTTPS connection to 198.51.100.23.
label: escalate
why: HARD CASE (no keywords). An email client launching mshta, a signed Windows binary that runs remote script, is a classic phishing execution chain (T1218.005).

text: Suricata ET INFO DNS query volume: 1,800 TXT lookups in 10 minutes to long random-looking subdomains of cdn-update.top from DEV-BUILD-01.
label: escalate
why: High-volume TXT queries with high-entropy labels to a fresh domain is the shape of DNS tunnelling, a covert channel for command and control or exfiltration (T1071.004).

text: Microsoft Defender: EICAR-Test-File detected as malware in C:\AVTest\eicar.com and quarantined on WS-IT-01.
label: close
why: HARD CASE (contains 'malware'). EICAR is a harmless industry test string. IT drops it monthly to prove AV is working, under change CHG-4471, and Defender quarantined it as designed.

text: Suricata ET EXPLOIT Apache Log4j RCE attempt (CVE-2021-44228) from 10.20.0.15 to WEB-01:443.
label: close
why: HARD CASE (contains 'exploit'). 10.20.0.15 is our authorised vulnerability scanner running its weekly scan; it is supposed to send Log4j probes.

text: Six failed logons (4625, bad password) for a.nguyen on WS-MKT-11 within 5 minutes, then a self-service password reset and successful logon from the same workstation.
label: close
why: A user who forgot their password on Monday morning: a handful of tries at their own desk, then the self-service reset. No remote source, no spray pattern.

text: PowerShell script block logging (4104): Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties MemberOf run by s.kim on ADMIN-JUMP-01 and exported to CSV.
label: close
why: s.kim is an IT administrator doing the quarterly access review, from the jump host that exists for exactly this. Enumeration by the right person from the right place.

text: CloudTrail: ConsoleLogin success with MFA for IAM user p.shah from 192.0.2.200 (hotel network); only DescribeInstances and ListBuckets calls followed.
label: close
why: A cloud engineer travelling to a conference, signing in with MFA and only reading. Unfamiliar IP, but strong authentication and nothing changed.

text: EDR: psexec.exe launched by svc_sccm from SCCM-01 against 40 workstations to run the November cumulative update installer.
label: close
why: The patching service account pushing the monthly update during the approved window CHG-4502. PsExec is an attacker favourite, but here it is the admin doing the job.
